Thanks for the SIG intake last week. As we complete our vendor review for AcmeCorp, we have a few follow-ups on access controls so we can close the identity chapter. Can you confirm the following for our SIG and provide any supporting artifacts?

1) SCIM: do you support SCIM 2.0? Does your SCIM flow include group->role syncing? How do you handle deprovisioning latency (time between IdP disable and Redwood account deactivation)?
2) SAML/SSO: do you support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SSO? Any constraints on assertions (NameID formats, audience, ACS endpoints)?
3) RBAC: what are your built-in roles and are they customizable? Can we map IdP groups to custom roles?
4) MFA & least privilege: Do you enforce MFA for console access or do you rely on the customer IdP? What is your recommended least-privilege baseline for admins/operators?

If possible, attach a simple CSV of your typical SCIM attribute mappings and a short note on token rotation for SCIM. We have a compliance window next Tuesday, so any docs by EOD Tuesday would be great.

From: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear list. TL;DR: yes to SCIM 2.0 with group->role mapping, SP+IdP SSO supported, RBAC is role-based with customizable mappings, and we recommend enforcing MFA at the IdP. See answers and artifacts attached.

Detailed answers below and attached: redwood_sig_answers_20270810.pdf and scim-attribute-mapping-20270810.csv

1) SCIM
- Protocol: We implement SCIM 2.0 (RFC 7644) for user and group provisioning.
- Group->Role mapping: Supported. The SCIM Groups endpoint can be mapped to Redwood roles; mapping is configured per-tenant in the private control plane or via a provisioning config in Dedicated/Hosted.
- Deprovisioning latency: When an IdP sets user to disabled, SCIM deprovisioning events are processed within our provisioning worker queue. Typical time-to-deactivate is under 60 seconds for Hosted, SLA-backed windows for Dedicated depend on your autoscale window (we document 1–2 minutes). We also provide an immediate on-demand disable API for emergency deprovisioning.
- Token rotation: SCIM tokens are long-lived API keys specific to the IdP integration. Customers can rotate tokens via the Console; we recommend rotation every 90 days. Audit logs show each token use and rotation event.

2) SAML/SSO
- Modes: We support both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SSO.
- Assertions: We accept NameID in email and persistent formats; recommended to use email for easiest mapping. Audience and ACS must match configured values in the Console; we validate audience and recipient.
- ACS/Entity constraints: Multiple ACS endpoints supported for subdomain setups; RelayState preserved.

3) RBAC
- Built-in roles: Viewer, Operator, Engineer, Admin. Roles are composable: you can add granular permissions (e.g., 'deploy_model', 'view_billing', 'manage_users').
- Custom roles: Supported on Dedicated and Private; Hosted supports role configurations per-account via the Console. Group->role mapping is configured via SCIM attributes or SAML assertion mapping (we support mapping both ways).
- Least privilege: For most customers we recommend: Admin (limit to SRE/security ops), Operator (day-to-day deployment), Engineer (model development), Viewer (read-only). Avoid giving Admin to product teams; prefer scoped Operator+custom perms.

4) MFA & least privilege baseline
- MFA: Redwood recommends enforcement at the customer IdP. For Hosted customers, we support enforcing SSO-only logins (no local passwords). For Private deployments we can integrate with customer-managed MFA/HSM solutions.
- Service accounts: Token-based service accounts are available; tokens can be scoped and have TTL. We recommend ephemeral tokens for orchestration and rotating long-lived tokens if required.

Next steps
- Attached: SCIM mapping CSV (attribute -> Redwood attribute; includes group->role examples) and our SIG answers PDF.
- If helpful, we can provide a short recording of SCIM mapping in the Console and schedule a 30-min call to walk through group->role mapping and deprovisioning tests.

Thanks — looping in Neha (Security) for anything technical I missed and Ben for procurement/contract alignment.

Thanks, Stephanie — adding a couple of operational clarifications from the infra side.

On deprovisioning: our worker queue acknowledges SCIM DELETE/PUT events and triggers immediate session invalidation for web console sessions and we invalidate KV caches for API tokens tied to an account. For API key sessions (service accounts) we mark tokens revoked and they fail auth within 10–30 seconds depending on edge cache propagation.

On group->role sync: by default we match on scim:group.displayName -> role name. For larger customers we can support a mapping table (see attached CSV) and a staging sync mode to preview role assignments prior to full sync.

On evidence: we can provide a short audit log extract showing a deprovisioning event (sanitized) — if you want that, let us know the time window and we will pull the export.
